Differentiation yields J_prime=6 log((1+r^2)/(1+r))/(pi^2 r)<0, and integrating at r=1 gives J~3(1-r)^2/(2pi^2). With known one-site p(r)=1/4-3 Li_2(r^2)/(2pi^2), p~3(1-r)log(1/(1-r))/pi^2; covariance is +3/16 at center, negative near one, hence at least one sign change. Independent high-precision quadrature compared with dilogarithmic formula at r=0,0.2,0.7,0.98 to ~1e-15; this is corroboration, the Fourier argument is the proof. No uniqueness of sign-change root follows.
